$comment: Weekly positioning book (PB-1.0, Saturday edition). Authored content from the executive brief and the internal research sidecar; live cushions and window status are computed in the app from the archive. Shadow book: no notional, no execution path; sizing weights withheld.
headline: Stocks reclaimed the break; bonds sold off with them.
view: The index broke its long average for one session and reclaimed it within two, while the ten-year rose with stocks on Friday and December hike pricing sat at 99%: the hawkish half of the label did the work, and the label held. The book tests only daily inputs: the front end above a tighter line, no re-break in structure, and the supply cushion through the producer meeting. Growth and inflation are not testable this window; the book stays de-grossed.

prior.note: Decided by the rules as pre-written; descriptive, not ledger evidence (the prior draft was never hashed).

legs.name: Front end above 4.50
legs.b: Two-year above 4.50 on all four window editions; low 4.61 on the core-inflation day, 4.69 at the close.

legs.name: Structure: no reclaim
legs.b: Lost on the first session as the index rose nearly 5%; Market Structure closed the week Technical neutral.

legs.name: Supply easing through the roll
legs.b: Supply Shock read Easing on every edition through the January roll, though Brent's January closed above $95.

tests.name: Front end
tests.rule: Two-year yield above 4.60 on every edition after 27 Nov through the first edition dated on or after 4 Dec; any edition at or below 4.60 falsifies.
tests.hypothesis: The hawkish half of the label holds a tighter line: with a December hike all but fully priced, core inflation at a two-year high and the ten-year rising with stocks, the two-year stays above 4.60.
tests.counter: Nine basis points of cushion; two hikes by January are two-thirds priced, so little hawkish news is left and a renewed equity slide would pull yields down.

tests.name: Structure
tests.rule: Market Structure reads anything other than Technical breakdown on every edition after 27 Nov through the first edition dated on or after 4 Dec.
tests.hypothesis: The 200-day break was a one-session event: the index reclaimed the line within two sessions and closed the week less than 1% under its long average.
tests.counter: The same chip names led both ways, the equal-weight index lagged on Friday, and the break line is 1.3% below Friday's close.

tests.name: Supply
tests.rule: Supply Shock reads Easing on every edition after 27 Nov through the first edition dated on or after 4 Dec; any other tag falsifies.
tests.hypothesis: The supply leg holds Easing through the producer meeting and a worse strike tape, with the reference six dollars under $90.
tests.counter: Brent's front contract is above $95 after the Ras Tanura and Jazan attacks; OPEC+ meets on 29 Nov, and a cut or a single refinery outage closes a six-dollar cushion in two sessions.

reserve: Held at the floor; deployed after the first resolution, along the surviving branch. All three exits rest on daily inputs (W-1).

notHeld.b: Falsified on Monday as the index rose nearly 5%; it broke again for one session on 25 Nov and closed neutral.
No dated release inside the window; W-1 admits a monthly basis only with a declared release. Core inflation printed before it.
The edge is named, firm against strong, but the tag crossed it three times in four sessions; a test would round-trip.
Weights revised on the completed class clock, with a possible new act class under review; gold swung 3% on alternate sessions.
The ten-year rose 9bp on Friday after eight straight declines; one session is not a turn.
Best week since April 2025 on a chip-led rally with Risk Sentiment still short of risk-on; the book stays de-grossed (since 30 Oct).

watch: OPEC+ meeting on Sunday 29 Nov (supply leg).
Whether the S&P holds above the −2% line to its 200-day (structure leg).
Class review of the Kuwait attack (scenario weights).

internal.commodity: Energy ELEVATED/FALLING on a firm dollar while prices lead commodities: keeps the supply cushion and the policy leg's inflation anchor, but the copper/gold lean is defensive, so the complex does not corroborate the equity reclaim.
